title: Find the Town Judge
statement: In a town of n people labeled 1 to n, the town judge trusts nobody and everybody else trusts the town judge. Return the label of the town judge, or -1 if none exists.
hints: Track net trust score = inDegree[i] - outDegree[i].
The town judge must have inDegree = n - 1 and outDegree = 0.
So net trust score equals exactly n - 1.

solutions.title: Degree Difference Array
Separate In/Out Arrays

editorial.approach: The town judge trusts nobody (out-degree 0) and is trusted by everyone else (in-degree n - 1). Compute the net trust score in_degree - out_degree for each person using a single array of size n + 1. For each trust pair [a, b], decrement score of a and increment score of b. The judge is the unique person with score n - 1.
editorial.why_optimal: Requires only a single pass over the trust array and one scan over people, taking O(N + E) time and O(N) space without needing full adjacency list structures.
editorial.pitfalls: Off-by-one errors from 1-based person indices. Forgetting that there can be at most one judge, and if multiple people satisfy the condition or none do, -1 must be returned.
